region.text: the territory the new state held in 1948 (the partition plan's Jewish state, 56% of Mandatory Palestine, plus ground won in the war)

ledger.note: 14 May 1948: Israel declares independence. 'Israel declared independence on 14 May 1948, shortly before the end of the mandate' (infobox 'Declaration of independence: 14 May 1948'); the 1948 War page gives the Jewish state 56% of Mandatory Palestine under the partition plan and dates the Mandate's expiry to 15 May 1948. No page gives a boundary; the region is Cliopatria's 1948 shape.

region.text: the Negev and the Gaza coast where the Egyptian army fought (same zone as the kingdom-of-egypt dossier)

ledger.note: 15 May 1948: Egypt invades. The page's infobox dates the war '15 May 1948 - 10 March 1949' and speaks of 'the four Arab armies that invaded on 15 May'; its territorial line lists 'Egyptian occupation of the Gaza Strip'. The zone is the one the kingdom-of-egypt dossier uses.

region.text: the West Bank including East Jerusalem

ledger.note: 15 May 1948: the Arab Legion enters the West Bank. The Legion 'fought only in the area that King Abdullah wanted to secure for Jordan: the West Bank, including East Jerusalem'; 'The IDF captured Lydda on 11 July'.

region.text: the Jordan Valley salients west of the Syrian border at the Sea of Galilee and Lake Huleh, 66 km2 of which stayed demilitarized under Syrian control

ledger.note: 1948: Syria holds ground west of the international border. The armistice page says 'Syria withdrew its forces from most of the territories it controlled west of the international border', so Syrian troops had crossed it; the page does not date the crossing (May is the 15 May invasion of the 1948 War page).

region.text: the Negev and the Gaza coast where the Egyptian army fought (same zone as the kingdom-of-egypt dossier)

ledger.note: 24 February 1949: Israel and Egypt sign the armistice at Rhodes. 'On 24 February the Israel-Egypt Armistice Agreement was signed in Rhodes'; 'Egypt remained in control of a strip of land along the coast, which became known as the Gaza Strip'; the 1948 War page adds that Israeli forces left the Sinai on 2 January 1949 and that the Egyptians agreed to negotiate a ceasefire on 7 January.

region.text: the Southern Negev down to the southern tip of Palestine

ledger.note: 10 March 1949: Israel reaches the Gulf of Aqaba. 'On 10 March, Israeli forces secured the Southern Negev, reaching the southern tip of Palestine' (Operation Uvda began on 5 March 1949); the page calls the region 'already designated to be part of the Jewish state in the UN Partition Plan', so the operation established sovereignty over land no state held.

region.text: the West Bank including East Jerusalem

ledger.note: 3 April 1949: Israel and Jordan sign the armistice. 'The agreement with Jordan was signed on 3 April 1949'; 'Jordanian forces remained in most positions held by them, particularly' in East Jerusalem and the Old City; the Green Line was demarcated.

region.text: Wadi Ara and the Little Triangle

ledger.note: April 1949: Wadi Ara and the Little Triangle pass to Israel. 'Israel received control in the area known as Wadi Ara' and the Little Triangle in the Jordan agreement, 'in exchange for territory in the southern hills of Hebron'. The page gives no day and no boundary; the region is the researcher's reading. [Reviewer me-10-j, 2026-10-25: region clipped to the side of the armistice line it lies on; the bare radius took in land on both sides.]

region.text: territory in the southern hills of Hebron

ledger.note: April 1949: Israel gives up land in the southern Hebron hills in exchange for Wadi Ara (same sentence as the gain above). [Reviewer me-10-j, 2026-10-25: region clipped to the side of the armistice line it lies on; the bare radius took in land on both sides.]

region.text: the Jordan Valley demilitarized zones

Lebanon signed on 23 March 1949; the page names no Israeli-held land in Lebanon.

region.text: the Sinai Peninsula and the Gaza Strip

region.text: the Sinai Peninsula and the Gaza Strip

The page gives no single date for the Israeli-Egyptian ceasefire.

region.text: the Sinai Peninsula and the Gaza Strip

region.text: the Golan Heights

region.text: the Israeli-held Golan Heights (the Golan Heights Law); Quneitra and the eastern third stayed Syrian after 1974

ledger.note: 14 December 1981: Israel annexes the Golan Heights. The Golan Heights Law extended Israeli law over the territory; UN Security Council Resolution 497 declared it 'null and void and without international legal effect', and the United States became the first state to recognise it in 2019. Contested sovereignty: the map draws it as Israeli de facto. [Reviewer me-10-j, 2026-10-25: region clipped to Cliopatria's Israel 1987 shape; the bare Golan polygon reaches 36.05 E and took in about 1,000 km2 that Syria held after the 1974 disengagement ('Civil administration of a third of the Golan Heights, including the capital Quneitra, was restored to Syria', Golan Heights page).]

wars.note: The war's own page was not opened (page budget).

wars.outcome: Begun by the 7 October 2023 attacks from Gaza; Israel invaded on 27 October 2023 and 'has occupied portions of the strip ever since'. Not ended at 2024.

certainty.note: The front lines moved all year; no armistice line existed before 1949. The Southern Negev frontier is open until 10 March 1949.

The 1949 armistice lines (the Green Line), the 1979 Egypt treaty and the 1994 Jordan treaty are line-defined. Exceptions: the Syrian demilitarized zones to 1967, East Jerusalem, the West Bank, the Golan Heights and the Lebanese belt, whose status is disputed or occupied; the Syrian buffer zone after December 2024.

notes: Written by me-10-j from nine pages (the page budget). SHAPES: Cliopatria draws every conquest as Israeli land (the Sinai 1956-1957 and 1967-1982 minus 1973-1975, Gaza 1956-1957, the West Bank and the Golan 1967-2024, Lebanon 1983-1986); the dossier keeps the state at the 1949 lines plus East Jerusalem and, from 14 December 1981, the Golan, and carries the rest as occupations. The 1973-1975 shape lacks the Sinai (wrong). Unexplained small steps: 1953 (-498 km2), 2006 (+1,602 km2), 2014 (-1,730 km2) (unverified: page budget). NOT READ (a gap-filler should open): Operation Yoav and Operation Hiram (October 1948 gains in the northern Negev and Galilee), the War of Attrition (1967-1970), Sinai I and II (1974, 1975), Oslo II and Areas A/B/C (1995), the Gaza disengagement page, the Israel-Jordan treaty (Israel's matching loss of Naharayim/Tzofar to Jordan, 26 October 1994; the kingdom-of-jordan dossier carries the gain), the 1982 Lebanon War page (month of invasion, Beirut). COUNTERPARTS: kingdom-of-egypt, kingdom-of-jordan, second-syrian-republic, republic-of-egypt and gaza-hamas have dossiers; arab-republic-of-egypt (the 1967-1982 Sinai counterpart; the 1967-1971 owner row is united-arab-republic) and syria (the Golan counterpart; the 1967-1972 row is arab-socialist-ba-ath-party) are used as one string each for the whole span; 'palestinians' is used for Gaza and the post-1988 West Bank as the generic Palestinian owner, as the united-arab-republic dossier does; british-mandate-for-palestine needs a dossier. Lebanon events 1948 (Israeli occupation of southern villages in October 1948, which the lebanon dossier records) are not entered: the pages opened do not date them.
